title: UPDATE: Anthropic Offers $25K Monthly Credits for Open Source Security
summary:
A program of financial support is now available to help software maintainers identify vulnerabilities in their code using artificial intelligence. Eligible organizations can receive $25,000 in usage credits per month for two months through Dec. 31, 2026, to utilize Anthropic's OSS Scanner. The tool now includes automatic fix verification that reopens issues if they recur, AI-generated threat models, and a new API with MCP connector support for repositories on GitHub and GitLab.

The AI-driven scanner has accepted 114 of 650 applicants, identifying 803 high-severity and 77 critical issues across millions of lines of code, including a high-severity memory-safety bug in curl (CVE-2026-92392). While the tool helps find long-standing flaws, reports from Axios indicate that some maintainers are being overwhelmed by the volume of AI-generated bug reports, which can bury legitimate security alerts.

11 days ago, our team @AnthropicAI launched OSS Scanner to give open source projects free, periodic vulnerability scans from our strongest models, inspired by OSS-Fuzz. Some numbers so far:
• ~650 projects applied
• 114 accepted
• 77 critical and 803 high model-rated findings reported (we haven’t scanned all projects yet)

How our reports ended up flagged as malware, and other learnings/updates below 🧵

A fix I'm excited about: curl, used by countless apps/devices to move data over the internet, just patched CVE-2026-92392. It's a high-severity memory-safety bug (a use-after-free) found with an early version of OSS Scanner.

@bagder called it one of curl's worst vulns in a long time, even if a crash is the likeliest outcome.

Thanks to Daniel and the curl team for fixing and writing it up so openly.

selectedTweets.text:
When a fix ships, Claude checks the changed code and marks the finding fixed, even if your team fixed it outside Claude Security. If the issue comes back, the finding reopens.

Each project also gets a threat model Claude writes from your code, which your team can edit.
